issues.description: The exercise specification and the reference solution consistently use the class name Meal as the core domain entity (e.g., UML and APIs: Meal, Meal[] orders, calculateTotalPrice(Meal), orderMeal(Meal)). However, the provided template repository does not contain a Meal implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java is empty) and instead contains an Order class (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Order.java) with the same fields/shape. The template's Main.java sample code (commented) also refers to Order. This name mismatch (Meal vs Order) will confuse students and can cause compilation or wiring problems: students following the problem statement will expect Meal to exist, but the template only provides Order, so code referring to Meal will not compile and students may either re-implement the wrong type or be blocked.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the core entity name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: provide a Meal.java implementation in the template that matches the reference solution (fields, constructor, and getters) and update/remove the template Order.java and any Main comments that reference Order. Alternatively, if Order is intended, update the problem statement, UML, and solution to use Order everywhere. Ensure the template compiles out-of-the-box with the names used in the problem description.
